display.title: Pesach and the Jewish Child: Why We Ask Questions at the Seder
display.summary_short: As Nissan approaches, Uncle Yossi explains why children are at the center of Pesach and why the Seder is built to get them asking questions.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given the week of Shabbos Mevarchim for Nissan. Uncle Yossi tells children that no holiday focuses on them like Pesach. From the start of the Pesach story, Pharaoh's decree targeted Jewish baby boys because he knew the children were the future of the Jewish people, and Hashem sent angels to save them. Today too, the whole Seder centers on the child: the Mah Nishtanah and dipping the karpas in salt water are there to make children ask. It is important not to be bashful but to ask, and the answers are found in the Torah, the Talmud, the Midrash and holy books. Parents and teachers must be ready to answer, as the Haggadah explains, and everything should be done with joy, as the Torah says, 'you shall rejoice in your festival'.
display.lesson: Don't be shy to ask questions; the answers are found in the Torah, and Pesach shows how precious every Jewish child is.
